problem: Resource-constrained multi-object navigation in ultra-large indoor scenes (>2,000 m^2) is handled poorly by prior switching heuristics: BFS-Global uses a rigid budget threshold blind to scene structure, and TFL-Reactive uses myopic triggers that cause ping-pong oscillation and waste travel budget. Exact SOP solvers are too slow for online use.
motivation: In kilometer-scale trajectories a single myopic decision can exhaust the whole travel budget, so global strategic planning is needed. SOP is a natural formulation for reward maximisation under a budget, but it is NP-hard and the expert solver (VNS) needs seconds, so it must be distilled into a fast network trained under the same partial observations as the agent to avoid teacher-student asymmetry.
key_idea: Formulate landmark exploitation as a Set Orienteering Problem and distill an offline VNS expert (run on partial observations) into a lightweight Transformer with geodesic-cost attention bias, refined by bounded 2-opt, alongside a heuristic frontier/exploitation switcher.
insight: Distilling the VNS expert gives a 94x speedup (41.03 ms vs 3861.42 ms) at a quality cost: Avg Reward 2014.5 vs 2753.2, and PPL 0.2258 vs 0.3231, so a sizeable gap to the teacher remains. Bounded 2-opt is cheap and useful: travel cost drops from 2435.6 to 2279.7 for +0.16 ms. Distance-bin probability visualisations suggest the geometric bias makes decoding prefer nearer nodes without becoming purely greedy. No ablation isolates the attention bias itself, so its contribution is supported only qualitatively.
method: Online semantic graph: builds a graph from a 0.1 m occupancy grid and detected landmarks of interest (LOIs), with nodes split into exploitation (LOI viewpoint sets) and exploration (frontier) modes.
Heuristic strategy switcher: a top-level rule using remaining budget, visit costs and exploration rate to switch from frontier exploration to SOP exploitation, avoiding mode toggling.

Conceptual SOP formulation: each LOI is a cluster of N_vp=5 candidate viewpoints, the top N_LOI=15 LOIs are kept, and the objective maximises cluster reward minus travel cost under budget B, visiting at most one viewpoint per set.
VNS expert teacher: solves the SOP offline over ProcTHOR layouts, using only the agent's online observation and map space, giving ~1e5 step-level transitions; deactivated online.

Strategic Transformer: 6-layer, 8-head, d=128 encoder over node features (x, y, reward); the normalised A* geodesic cost matrix is added to attention as log(c_hat + eps) (Graphormer-style bias); a pointer-style autoregressive head with masking decodes greedily; trained by behavioral cloning with teacher forcing.
Bounded 2-opt refinement: at most 100 iterations on the capped graph, with inter-set reordering and intra-set viewpoint swapping.
Budget and Traversability gates: the Budget Gate stops the tour when accumulated odometry cost reaches B; the Traversability Gate detects risk in unobserved regions using the online grid map.

setting.backbone: Strategic Transformer (6-layer encoder, 8 heads, d=128, pointer decoder), trained from scratch by behavioral cloning; heuristic switcher and frontier exploration are rule-based
setting.training_data: ~1e5 step-level state-action transitions generated by an offline VNS SOP expert on procedural ProcTHOR layouts
setting.observation: egocentric 90° FoV with simulator instance-segmentation masks, simulator pose, online 2D occupancy grid (0.1 m/pixel)
setting.action_space: high-level selection of the next viewpoint node in an SOP tour, executed with A* path planning; frontier navigation in exploration mode
setting.privileged: simulator-provided pose and instance segmentation masks; the teacher is restricted to online observations; object co-occurrence statistics come from offline expert trajectories

numbers.eval_set_note: 90 validation episodes over 9 target categories, ~50-room houses >2,000 m^2
numbers.extra: distilled from VNS expert; simulator pose and instance segmentation

numbers_note: Custom ProcTHOR benchmark (90 episodes); no standard benchmark reported. Solver-level results: Transformer-SOP+2-opt Avg Reward 2014.5, Avg Cost 2279.7, 41.03 ms; VNS-SOP 2753.2, 2216.8, 3861.42 ms.
results: On the custom ultra-large ProcTHOR benchmark, BF-SOP with the Strategic Transformer gets PPL 0.2258, beating TFL-Reactive (0.1862), BFS-Global (0.1796) and Nearest Frontier (0.1059). The VNS teacher reaches 0.3231, so a large gap remains. Inference takes 41.03 ms, a 94.11x speedup over VNS.
limitations: Large gap to the VNS teacher (PPL 0.2258 vs 0.3231; reward 2014.5 vs 2753.2); distillation fails in complex cul-de-sacs by overestimating rewards

Small evaluation (90 episodes, 9 categories, one simulator), only weak re-implemented baselines, and no ablation of the geometric attention bias or the switcher; relies on simulator pose and instance segmentation, no real-robot test
Capped at 15 LOIs and 5 viewpoints, chosen by the expert solver's tractability; switcher is heuristic and the reward is not learned
